_about: Grounded coaching knowledge base generated from human-readable Markdown indicator cards. The LLM must describe measured metrics without inventing causes, diagnoses, shot outcomes, or corrections.

indicator card.label: short friendly label shown to the user
indicator card.measures: what the number physically measures (one sentence, plain)
indicator card.why: why it matters to a golfer (one sentence, plain, non-prescriptive)
indicator card.in_range_phrasing: approved description when the metric is inside the tour band
indicator card.out_low_phrasing: approved neutral description when below the tour band (null if not noteworthy low)
indicator card.out_high_phrasing: approved neutral description when above the tour band (null if not noteworthy high)
indicator card.glosses: term -> approved short gloss, for any jargon used in this card
indicator card.swing_phase_display: human-readable swing phase from the Markdown source
indicator card.evidence_classification: directly measured, derived comparison, and unsupported claims
indicator card.comparison_language: approved neutral phrases for comparing two swings
indicator card.allowed_inferences: claims the LLM may make from this metric
indicator card.prohibited_inferences: claims the LLM must not make from this metric
indicator card.approved_examples: approved response examples grouped by situation
indicator card.prohibited_examples: response examples the LLM must not produce
indicator card.handedness_note: optional handedness limitation for side-specific metrics

glossary.tour range: the typical spread of values seen across professional tour swings
glossary.tour median: the middle value among professional tour swings
glossary.address: the setup position, just before the swing starts
glossary.top: the top of the backswing, where the club changes direction
glossary.impact: the instant the club meets the ball
glossary.backswing: the takeaway and turn back, away from the target
glossary.downswing: the move from the top of the backswing down to the ball
glossary.percentile: where this swing sits relative to tour pros — e.g. 30th percentile means 30% of pros are lower
glossary.shoulder turn: How much the upper body rotates during the backswing.
glossary.tour reference range: The typical spread of measured values seen across the professional swings used for comparison.
glossary.top of the backswing: The point where the backswing ends and the downswing begins.
glossary.hip turn: How much the lower body rotates during the backswing.
glossary.shoulder–hip separation: The difference between how far the shoulders rotate and how far the hips rotate.
glossary.x-factor: Another name for shoulder–hip separation at the top of the backswing.
glossary.hip rotation at impact: How far the hips have turned toward the target when the club reaches the ball.
glossary.open hips: Hips rotated to face more toward the target.
glossary.spine angle: How much the upper body leans away from an upright position.
glossary.upper-body lean: The angle of the torso relative to standing upright.
glossary.posture: The upper-body and spine angle held during the swing.
glossary.posture change: The difference in upper-body angle between setup and impact.
glossary.setup: The golfer’s starting position before the swing begins.
glossary.head sway: Sideways movement of the head during the swing.
glossary.sideways movement: Movement across the camera view rather than up or down.
glossary.percent of body height: A body-size-adjusted way of expressing movement distance.
glossary.head height change: Upward or downward movement of the head during the swing.
glossary.vertical movement: Movement up or down in the camera view.
glossary.lead arm: The arm closer to the target.
glossary.lead-arm extension: How straight the lead arm appears during the swing.
glossary.arm bend angle: The measured angle used to describe how bent or straight the arm is.
glossary.trail arm: The arm farther from the target.
glossary.arm bend: How much the elbow joint is folded.
glossary.folded arm: An arm position with more bend at the elbow.
glossary.lead knee: The knee closer to the target.
glossary.knee flex: How much the knee joint is bent.
glossary.hip shift: Sideways movement of the pelvis during the swing.
glossary.toward the target: Movement in the direction the golfer intends to hit the ball.
glossary.tempo: The timing relationship between the backswing and downswing.
glossary.tempo ratio: The backswing duration divided by the downswing duration.
glossary.three-to-one ratio: A backswing that takes about three times as long as the downswing.
glossary.hand speed: How quickly the hands travel during the swing.
glossary.impact area: The part of the swing immediately around the moment the club reaches the ball.
glossary.peak speed: The highest measured speed during the selected part of the swing.
glossary.body-lengths per second: A body-size-adjusted speed unit that expresses movement relative to the golfer’s height or scale.
glossary.normalized by body size: Adjusted relative to the golfer’s body dimensions to support comparison across golfers.

shoulder_turn_top_deg.label: Shoulder turn
shoulder_turn_top_deg.plain_name: How far the shoulders rotate at the top
shoulder_turn_top_deg.measures: Measures how far the shoulders rotated away from the target by the top of the backswing.
shoulder_turn_top_deg.beginner_explanation: Shoulder turn describes how much the upper body rotated during the backswing.
shoulder_turn_top_deg.why: This measurement helps describe how the upper body moved during the backswing. It does not determine whether the movement was correct or what caused it.

shoulder_turn_top_deg.out_low_phrasing: The measured shoulder turn was below the tour reference range at the top of the backswing.
shoulder_turn_top_deg.out_high_phrasing: The measured shoulder turn was above the tour reference range at the top of the backswing.

approved_examples.Above the reference range: Your measured shoulder turn was above the tour reference range at the top of the backswing. That means the upper body rotated farther than the comparison range in this measurement.
approved_examples.Comparison — increased: Your measured shoulder turn increased compared with the earlier swing. This describes how the two measured swings differed; it does not by itself mean the current movement was better.
